title: These Lifts BUILT My Physique (Top 10 Hypertrophy List)
summary: NH ranks the ten lifts that built his physique, from French press at 10 to push-ups at 1. The top three (push-ups, pull-ups, sit-ups) are equipment-free basics he did for years, and he argues the bare minimum for a bodybuilding program is a 'big ten' of patterns covering every body part.
claims: The French press built most of his triceps long head, a part he neglected for years
Dumbbell French press can cause elbow tendonitis, which stops you spamming and progressing it; the cable French press is S tier and shifting the torso angle makes it more comfortable
He regrets neglecting Romanian deadlifts; doing 80% of hinge volume with deadlifts and 20% with RDLs is wrong if hypertrophy is the goal
The RDL plateaus on the concentric because the eccentric is never limiting, so keep doing some deadlifts alongside RDLs to progress the hinge pattern
All of his shoulder gains in the past 3-4 months came from spamming the overhead press; without vertical pressing you shortchange your shoulders and lateral raises are not enough
Pick whatever overhead press grip or implement is comfortable (narrow, snap, behind the neck, dumbbells, neutral) as long as the arm moves overhead
Two-arm bent-over dumbbell rows were his only posterior chain exercise for about two years, and his first real deadlift was 275 lb for 5 with good form
People who dislike dumbbell rows have not done them properly or found their style yet
You cannot build legs as big as possible without a squat or heavy knee-flexion pattern; any variant (low bar, SSB, hack, belt squat) works
He had 26-27 inch quads purely from squats before he ever did leg extensions or other methods
If more people treated curls as seriously as compounds there would be many more people with big arms
Pullovers, only done for three years, produced a ribcage expansion effect he calls almost magical; if he could go back he would make his younger self do them first
Daily sit-ups as a kid with feet hooked under furniture are why he still has a six-pack; not doing ab isolation is a mistake you will regret
Pull-ups are still the king of upper back builders; once you can't add reps, add weight, use towels or change grip
A pull-up variation, rows, dumbbell rows and pullovers plus a hinge like the RDL cover all upper back gains
Push-ups made the single biggest difference to his physique: he did hundreds every day with no rest days, and abandoning them for the bench press was a mistake
Ring push-ups, elevated, are a hard variation he uses for upper chest and shoulders
A real base is proficiency at push-ups and pull-ups, not a four-plate deadlift; his novice program has more push-ups than bench
Never abandon the basics that gave you most of your gains, even when advanced; refine and add on top of them
The bare minimum for a bodybuilding program is a 'big ten' covering every body part, not a big three or five
exercises: cable stack preferred; shift torso angle to press behind head
long head triceps; dumbbells risk tendonitis
any comfortable grip, arm goes overhead
bent over two-arm, now one-arm braced
high bar, low bar, SSB, hack, belt squat
